Explicit sensitive Cookie headers therefore persist across the stated cross-origin redirect. The patch adds Cookie to the default set. This does not assert browser cookie-jar behavior or override user-defined policies. Raw CVE, repair parent, and selected CNA metric match.
limitations: No HTTP execution; applications that disable redirects or remove Cookie explicitly are outside the label.
The retained CNA score differs from reviewed GitHub's later CVSS4 rating; the declared CNA-first selection is followed.

judgments.rationale: At the retained v8.5.1 release, the untrusted decoded header is passed to the key callback; explicitly configured algorithms suppress PEM-based inference, and verification checks algorithm membership before passing the same public-key bytes to jws.verify without key-type compatibility enforcement. The stated mixed-algorithm, poorly bound callback and known-public-key assumptions support the narrowed HMAC confusion claim. The causal repair is inferred through the retained release comparison: ecdf6 adds KeyObjects and rejects HS with non-secret keys; the advisory links a later release commit. This is not misrepresented as a first-parent mapping. CNA severity agrees.
limitations: Static key/algorithm flow only; no forged token was generated or verified.
Default PEM algorithm inference alone does not establish this misconfiguration.
Repair mapping is an explicit release-history inference, not a direct advisory link to ecdf6.

judgments.rationale: The nonempty key regex combined with search from the current position can skip a leading equals sign and reinterpret the value of a nameless cookie as a named cookie. The public parser only discards empty parsed keys, so it does not restore the lost distinction. The repair permits empty keys, anchors matching at the current offset and skips empty names. The label correctly requires affected browser/subdomain behavior and application selection of the malicious value, rather than universal browser impact. Direct mapping, first parent and CNA metric match.
limitations: No browser or cookie-parser execution; browser acceptance and duplicate-cookie ordering remain explicit deployment conditions.

judgments.rationale: The vulnerable parser selects registered parsers by substring search over the full Content-Type string; application/json precedes text/plain, so a JSON substring in parameters of a browser-safelisted essence can select the JSON parser. The run/done path delivers the parsed body to the handler. The repair parses MIME type and distinguishes its essence from parameters. The label requires a JSON/preflight-dependent state-changing route, credential-bearing browser behavior and no independent CSRF defense. The direct CVE mapping, parent and CNA severity agree.
limitations: No browser request or route execution; independent CSRF/origin defenses and SameSite policy can prevent exploitation.

judgments.rationale: is_content_type strips parameters but compares the essence case-sensitively. is_form_content_type feeds that result into respond's cross-origin state-changing-method guard, so an uppercase equivalent can bypass that guard. The repair lowercases the essence. The selected POST allegation is narrower than the guard's full method set and preserves accepting endpoint, credential and independent-defense conditions. The pinned parent, direct CVE repair reference and CNA metric agree.
limitations: Static server guard assessment; no browser behavior was executed, and the advisory's cookie/browser conditions remain necessary.

judgments.rationale: Re-reviewed the corrected frozen accepted span311–335 against the pinned source and repair. It now exactly contains the admin:users PATCH handler: attacker-supplied admin is assigned at325–329 and assign_default_roles at330–331 grants the built-in admin role through roles.py283–284. The repair explicitly rejects granting admin without current_user.admin. The original broad292–355 span was revised; its initial revise judgment remains in astra-decisions-b-v1.json and astra-notes-b-v1.md. Identity, vulnerable pin, direct repair mapping, narrowed location, conditional escalation mechanism and CNA severity are supported.
limitations: No authenticated API request was executed; admin:users is already highly privileged and scope filters must permit the chosen account.

judgments.rationale: HubAuthenticated obtains a token from URL or Authorization header, validates it, and for token-authenticated HubOAuth requests persists that token into a cookie. Consequently a still-active JupyterLab tab using the page-config token can reissue a single-user credential cookie after another tab's logout. The repair limits persistence to URL tokens and clears PageConfig.token when loading server extensions. The label properly excludes restoration of Hub login. First-parent mapping, advisory and CNA severity agree.
limitations: No multiple-tab browser session was executed; this assessment is limited to single-user-server cookie reinstatement.

judgments.rationale: The beta-pin IPC decoder constructs InvokeRequest from a frame message and dispatches it without an invoke-key requirement; on_message reaches capability resolution without a frame-initialization binding. The patch adds the runtime key to both transports and rejects a mismatching key before dispatch. Existing ACL checks still apply to plugin commands/app manifests, so the label's reachable meaningful-command assumption is material and appropriately avoids claiming unrestricted native execution. The retained GitHub advisory directly references this repair and explains parent-frame IPC exposure. Parent and CNA metric match.
limitations: No WebView execution; script execution in the remote iframe and a command reachable through the resulting ACL resolution are required.
The invoke key is a subframe boundary, not protection against a compromised initialized main WebView.

judgments.rationale: The endpoint resolves and checks only the initially requested path, then calls recursive read_dir without scope. Its metadata-based is_dir follows symlinks, and recursion descends into such child paths without another scope check, exposing entry metadata outside the allowed tree. The patch threads scope into recursion and checks symlink destinations. The label correctly restricts impact to directory listings and requires an accessible out-of-scope target and an existing crafted link. Advisory repair linkage and parent are supported; CNA severity is retained despite a lower GitHub rating.
limitations: No filesystem traversal executed; no arbitrary file-content disclosure is claimed.
CNA8.3 is copied per policy; the reviewed GitHub5.8 disagreement remains disclosed.

judgments.rationale: VerifyGet immediately returns through ctx.Error when GetOriginalURL fails; Error only sets JSON content/body and logging, leaving the successful HTTP status unchanged. The same source shows URL parsing of forwarded/original headers and ReplyUnauthorized's explicit401 status. The repair substitutes ReplyUnauthorized on that failure path, matching the advisory's nginx auth_request status-based authorization bypass. The label explicitly requires a proxy that forwards the malformed value and still routes the outer request. Direct mapping, pin and CNA metric match.
limitations: No nginx integration or malformed request was executed; other proxies/normalization may reject the request first.

judgments.rationale: DoesSessionSatisfy trusts valid cached AvailableAAL and accepts an aal1 session when that cache understates available assurance. For unset values it recomputes through credential counters, but the code strategy lacks the active-credential counter interface at this pin, consistent with the code-only first-factor assumptions. Settings and whoami callers use this gate. The actual repair123e8078 adds code counters and refreshes understated assurance; its message links the advisory, unlike later empty documentary commits. The label preserves OTP possession, configured second factor and highest_available conditions and does not assert an elevated session AAL. CNA severity agrees.
limitations: No OTP login or second-factor flow was executed; stale available_aal and code-only first-factor configuration are essential.
The broad repair includes unrelated credential normalization; acceptance concerns only the described assurance gate.

judgments.rationale: getServiceUrlFromHeaders gives attacker-forwarded x-zitadel-forward-host priority over ZITADEL_API_URL. createServiceForHost obtains server credentials and forwards that destination into transport creation; the unauthenticated loginname page invokes backend settings/org helpers with it. The repair binds the transport base URL to the configured API and separates tenant/public metadata. The label appropriately limits the finding to destination control under proxy-header and egress assumptions, rather than asserting arbitrary response disclosure. Direct CVE mapping, parent and CNA severity agree.
limitations: No network request executed; reverse-proxy stripping/overwriting and egress controls can block this path.
Full response-byte disclosure is outside this narrowed static label.

judgments.rationale: Certificate-chain construction uses the leaf NotBefore timestamp, while verifyInternal later calls CheckExpiry only with the leaf and a trusted timestamp or current time. CheckExpiry compares only that certificate's bounds. A custom chain whose issuer expires before its leaf can therefore pass these checks at a time after issuer expiry, assuming signature/policy/transparency checks otherwise pass. The patch carries the built issuing chain to CheckExpiry and checks each issuer at the observation time. The label explicitly excludes public Sigstore PKI. Direct repair mapping, parent and CNA severity agree.
limitations: No certificates or signatures were generated or verified; a customized PKI with the stated validity mismatch is required.
Trusted timestamp selection is not assumed attacker-forgeable.

judgments.rationale: The pinned filter parser resolves field metadata and translates direct/composite/relation predicates without checking field read permissions. The find-many query runner applies caller filters to both result and aggregation builders, while output-read restrictions are enforced separately; this supports a predicate oracle over otherwise permitted rows. The direct patch checks object/field readability before translation and filters unreadable saved-view fields. The label preserves record access and observable/guessable-domain assumptions, avoiding direct field output or cross-tenant claims. CNA CVSS4.0 is correctly preferred over GitHub's3.1 because the CNA has a numeric score.
limitations: No GraphQL/REST query executed; inference requires observable results and suitable candidate values.
The source CNA7.1 CVSS4 rating and GitHub6.5 CVSS3.1 rating are distinct; no scores were recomputed.

judgments.rationale: The pinned resolver's plain TypeORM query selects shared core.agentTurn rows only by agentId and loads messages/parts. Class guards validate the caller's workspace and AI setting permission, not ownership of the argument. The stored entity has an explicit workspaceId, and the repair passes authenticated workspaceId into a wrapper whose find merges that predicate. Release2.9 explicitly includes the repair PR, supporting the clearly labeled inferred CVE mapping. The current label is appropriately read-only and requires known victim agent UUID, multiple workspaces and caller permissions; it does not need the evaluation mutation or LLM execution. CNA severity agrees.
limitations: No tenant query executed; UUID discovery/guessing is not established and must not be inferred.
Mapping is release-plus-source inference rather than a direct advisory-to-commit reference; only the read endpoint is assessed.

decisions.reason: The published CVE and GHSA identify userinfo/authority confusion and link PR 1561; the raw PR commit list contains ebdeb613 and its parent is the exported pin. navigate_to applies the guard before page.goto. With allowed.test in allowed_domains, https://allowed.test:pw@blocked.test/ yields the allowed authority prefix while its hostname is blocked.test. The patch switches to hostname. The source location is the actual authorization guard. The CNA 4.0 CVSS 3.1 rating is accurately selected over the conflicting GitHub 9.3 rating.

The published advisory directly names fix 8595237 and the model-generated cwd sandbox error; its parent matches the export. ExecParams.cwd is passed to both sandbox constructors at the reporting location. Additional pinned caller inspection found ShellToolCallParams.workdir joined into cwd, and WorkspaceWrite adds that cwd to writable roots. Patch hunks separate command_cwd from turn_context.cwd and feed the latter into policy construction. This supports the scoped workspace authority-confusion label, with the CNA CVSS 4.0 score 8.6 copied accurately.

CVE/GHSA directly link the exact fix and vulnerable source revision. GetRequestURI preserves query text (or the configured forwarded URI), and isAllowedPath applies the skip-route regex to it; isAllowedRoute and IsAllowedRequest use that decision to skip authentication. A broad expression such as ^/api/.*/status can match /api/private?x=/status although the backend path is private. Both reported locations carry this flow. The patch substitutes path-only extraction. Published CNA CVSS 3.1 9.1 matches the label.

The published CVE and GHSA identify the clientSession route and the GHSA references fix 014007c; metadata makes the exported revision its parent. Encoder.deserialize wraps caller bytes in ApplicationObjectInputStream and calls readObject. The GHSA supplies the request/JATO rendering trace; read-only inspection of the bundled jato-2005-05-04.jar independently found getParameter("jato.clientSession"), decodeHttp64 and Encoder.deserialize calls, and ApplicationObjectInputStream.resolveClass loading named classes without a whitelist. The pinned IOUtils implementation uses WhitelistObjectInputStream, consistent with the patch delegation. The sink location supports unsafe deserialization under the declared endpoint/filter assumptions. CNA CVSS 4.0 9.3 is supported.

CVE and GHSA describe importChatflows id injection; the GHSA PR 4226 and its metadata bind fix f963e5a, whose parent is the export. Pinned route/controller inspection confirms POST importchatflows passes req.body.Chatflows to this service. The service quotes each supplied id without escaping, then interpolates the concatenated list into QueryBuilder.where before subsequent flowData parsing. Caller permission to import does not authorize SQL syntax. The patch validates UUIDs before query construction, not parameterization. CNA CVSS 3.1 6.5 is the stated selection despite alternate CNA 4.0 and GitHub scores.

The CVE directly maps to aee3fb1, whose parent is the exported pin. ParseXMLResponse unmarshals a Response independently from the etree tree; validateXMLResponse calls validateSigned but consumes resp.Assertion. findChild returns the first matching child, so validateSigned can check a different Assertion from the identity object populated by unmarshalling a multiple-assertion response. The reporting location implements that incomplete signature check. The patch parses each assertion from the same element it validates and returns a validated assertion; its TestMultipleAssertions is corroborating unexecuted regression evidence. CNA CVSS 3.1 9.1 is supported.

CVE 8124 links issue 480533, whose raw report identifies glm_source and the same scan/flatten line. The 17.3.1 tag record binds df018582; this version is affected, and the release comparison contains fix 878cda6. preferred_language reaches marketing_site_language when no valid preference cookie short-circuits it; scan materializes every locale match and flatten allocates another collection. The patch replaces this with an anchored marketing-host match and bounded captures. Both entry and allocation locations are relevant. CNA CVSS 3.1 7.5 is supported.

Published CVE/release text identifies CI_JOB_TOKEN-to-session escalation. The release tag binds affected 17.3.1 to the export, and the comparison contains cafae257, whose security branch/message specifically describes the job-token exchange. Pinned JWT authentication callers resolve usable build tokens to the build user; dependency-proxy tokens contain user_id. At both reporting locations the controller resolves that user and calls sign_in, excluding project bots/service accounts rather than preserving restricted job scope. The patch installs StripCookies for /v2 before ActionDispatch::Cookies, addressing session-cookie issuance. CNA CVSS 3.1 6.7 is supported.

CVE 6685 links issue 472012; its disclosure states only Maintainers/Owners should view group runners and identifies the GraphQL information path. The affected 17.3.1 tag binds the export and the comparison contains fix 084025e, whose branch includes issue 472012. RunnerPolicy admits Developer group/project associations and grants read_runner in the reported rules; anonymous prevention does not block authenticated Developers. The patch raises these association thresholds to Maintainer. Both locations support the scoped information-disclosure label. CNA CVSS 3.1 3.1 is supported.

Re-review of the changed packet supports its narrowed Local.Path-to-mklink claim. The published CVE and issue 121879 map to PR 121881/merge 620bc81; the export is its first parent and the CNA CVSS 3.1 score 7.2 is accurately retained. Pinned local.go NewMounter/getGlobalLocalPath propagate Local.Path for a directory, then SetUpAt checks backsteps and mount state before MakeAbsolutePath and MountSensitiveWithoutSystemd. The Windows wrapper delegates to MountSensitive, whose bind branch normalizes slash/drive syntax but does not remove cmd metacharacters; mklinkSource then reaches cmd /c mklink at the sole reporting location. The patch replaces shell invocation with os.Symlink. The revision explicitly excludes the unestablished rmdir target allegation, resolving the original location blocker. Acceptance is conditional on the stated Local.Path reaching this helper, including the preceding file-type and mount-state checks; it does not assert that an arbitrary nonexistent injected path reaches the sink.

The CVE and official issue describe envFrom omission in all three container classes. Issue 124336 cites the relevant PR family, and fix 7c861b1 is the release cherry-pick containing exactly these guards, with the exported pin as parent. Validate dispatches ephemeral-container updates separately and applies enforced mountable-secret checks on pod creation. The reported loops validate Env.SecretKeyRef but omit EnvFrom.SecretRef, enabling an unlisted named secret to cross the policy boundary. The patch adds the omitted allowlist check to init, ordinary and ephemeral loops. CNA CVSS 3.1 2.7 matches.

CVE and issue 91542 identify half-blind controller SSRF and map master to PR 89794/merge 01df16a, whose parent is the export. StorageClass resturl populates p.url; CreateVolume constructs the Heketi client and propagates VolumeCreate errors. Pinned vendor inspection confirms POST to host+/volumes and response-body-to-error conversion. Provision returns the error, and the controller emits it in a claim event at the third reporting location. The patch removes client error detail from events while retaining outbound requests. All three locations support the scoped request-plus-disclosure chain. CNA CVSS 3.1 6.3 is correctly selected.

Published CVE/GHSA map the scheduler local-settings problem to PR 41672 and the backported commit 03e01e7; its parent matches the export. initialize calls prepare_syspath before import_local_settings. prepare_syspath adds the DAG folder, and import_local_settings executes import airflow_local_settings, so a DAG author can supply scheduler configuration code under the stated no-earlier-shadowing assumption. The patch splits path setup and delays adding the DAG folder until after this import. Each reported location participates in that order-dependent boundary crossing. CNA has textual important severity only, so the declared fallback to GitHub reviewed CVSS 3.1 8.8 is supported.

CVE/GHSA describe DAG-author script-bearing descriptions and link PR 35460/fix 0b995602, whose parent is the export. The trigger view copies DAG parameters and marks description_html/custom_html_form as Markup without sanitizing; the pinned trigger template renders those fields into the page. A distinct authorized viewer therefore crosses the author-to-browser trust boundary. The patch adds allow_raw_html_descriptions defaulting False and removes/trust-gates raw HTML. The reported Markup location is causally relevant. CNA textual low and GitHub reviewed CVSS 3.1 5.4 differ; the label correctly uses its declared numeric fallback.

CVE/GHSA link the unauthenticated validate/code issue to PR 6911 and faac4db, whose parent matches the exported pin. The APIRouter endpoint has no active-user dependency and passes code.code to validate_code. The helper compiles and execs FunctionDef nodes; Python definition-time expressions/decorators can execute even though ordinary function bodies are not called. Pinned router inspection confirms validate_router inclusion without an added dependency. Both entry and helper locations are relevant. The patch adds CurrentActiveUser rather than a code sandbox. CNA CVSS 3.1 9.8 is supported.

CVE/GHSA link creation-endpoint traversal to PR 12337; its metadata binds merge 41d34b2 and the exported first parent. The endpoint accepts a current user and a name string, only strips spaces/checks length, then joins name with root/user and mkdirs before writing embedding_metadata.json. Absolute paths replace the prefix and parent components escape it. The existing _resolve_kb_path containment helper is not used on this creation path. The patch resolves the user and candidate paths and checks is_relative_to before creation. The location includes the actual writes. Published CNA CVSS 3.1 6.5 is copied faithfully, including its explicitly disclosed PR:N versus authenticated-endpoint inconsistency.

The published CVE/GHSA directly reference fix 2b4b1dc, whose parent is the export, and describe ChatOpenAI image token counting. The entry loops over image_url content and calls _url_to_size unless detail is low. That helper checks dependency availability and URL syntax, then directly calls httpx.get without restricting destination; the fetch precedes image decoding. Both reported spans include the relevant operations. The patch adds validate_safe_url and an image-fetch opt-out. CNA CVSS 3.1 3.7 matches the label.

CVE/GHSA directly map legacy prompt loading to 27add913, whose parent is the exported pin. load_prompt_from_config dispatches into helpers that read template_path or examples paths without absolute/parent-component rejection. The few-shot loader propagates paths through templates, nested example prompts and examples, then returns the loaded contents in prompt objects. Extension/format checks limit which files can be exposed but do not impose containment. The patch validates these paths by default and propagates an explicit dangerous-path opt-in. Both reporting locations support the conditional file-read/disclosure chain. CNA CVSS 3.1 7.5 is supported.

The external router invokes the internal-header filter, but its list omits x-middleware-subrequest. The sandbox counts attacker-supplied repetitions of the middleware name and returns x-middleware-next before executing middleware at depth five. Both the omitted filter and early-return guard are relevant. The directly referenced repair filters chains lacking the process-specific internal identifier. Source at the verified parent supports middleware-only authorization bypass under the declared reachable-header and endpoint assumptions. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 9.1 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The pinned base server treats x-now-route-matches as evidence of SSG even for the scoped SSR Pages Router route. The SSR renderer calls getServerSideProps without setting zero revalidation, and base-server substitutes one second when the result omits revalidate. These three spans form the input, missing non-cacheability assignment, and cache-duration propagation. The directly referenced repair sets SSR revalidate to zero and removes the fallback. Shared-cache/content consequences remain deployment-dependent. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 7.5 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The route map stores literal parameterized patterns; ServeHTTP fast-matches the literal request path and invokes its leaf with nil parameters. The unguarded public snapshot API passes the resulting empty key to the ORM struct lookup, which lacks an explicit key restriction; the CNA confirms snapshot disclosure for this literal path. The repair disables that shortcut for parameter markers and rejects an empty key. All three source spans support the deliberately narrowed reading claim; expiry handling and deletion distinctions are retained. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 9.8 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

OAuth SyncUser passes external identity, email and login into UpsertUser. After external-ID and email misses, LookupByOneOf resolves the attacker-controlled login to the victim; LookupAndUpdate then associates the external authentication record. The intervening user-mapping policy is explicit and OSS permits it. The repair gives OAuth email-only lookup parameters. CVE-to-fix mapping is an inference supported by the exact repair in the retained v9.0.2...v9.0.3 comparison and the matching CNA mechanism/fixed release, not a direct advisory commit link. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 7.1 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

GetDetailedProject enforces projects/get, then returns the helper-provided repositories without sanitization. Traced helpers retrieve project-indexed secrets and copy passwords, tokens and private keys into repository objects. The direct advisory-linked repair sanitizes each repository and cluster before returning them. The accepted server location is the actual disclosure boundary. The scoped claim requires project-scoped repository credentials and projects/get, not merely application management permissions. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 10 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The terminal entry checks applications/get and exec/create before opening the session. Subsequent websocket Read checks token validity and refresh but performs no RBAC recheck before accepting stdin. Removing exec permission alone need not invalidate the token, so the declared already-open session remains usable. The direct repair passes RBAC state into the session and checks both permissions during reads. The labeled read span is causally relevant without asserting bypass of initial authentication. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 4.7 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The maintainer role explicitly grants metadata create/update/delete. The metadata handlers enforce these grants, resolve the same project, validate metadata and perform mutations, so the guard exists but authorizes a role that should lack configuration authority. The repair removes exactly those grants. Mapping is inferred from the matching maintainer advisory and v2.10.2...v2.10.3 comparison containing this precise repair; the unrelated commit subject is not treated as proof. Same-project scope is supported. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 6.4 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The catalog regex matches only the path without a trailing slash. The slash variant therefore adds no catalog requirement to accessList, and the authorization caller iterates the empty list successfully. The direct repair adds the optional trailing slash. Both the matcher and access-list propagation spans are relevant. The declared downstream route/proxy compatibility is necessary; the consequence is repository-name disclosure, not image or credential access. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 5.3 (github_reviewed_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The update handler first evaluates explicit administrative permission, but on failure accepts matching parent identity and proceeds to parse NewPolicy and update the service account. IAM evaluation applies parent authority and inline restrictions, explaining why a restricted enabled child can alter its restriction toward its stronger parent. The direct repair removes the same-parent fallback and evaluates inline policy without owner bypass. Both the handler guard and policy propagation spans contribute to the narrow escalation claim. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 8.8 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The chunk reader fills and returns caller buffers before reaching the advertised chunk boundary where the signature is checked. The upload handler derives size from decoded-content-length and the hash reader limits consumption to that size, so the declared oversized chunk can leave the verifier unreached. Seed request authentication and PUT authorization still occur. The directly referenced repair reads a bounded whole chunk, verifies its signature, then returns its bytes. The source span supports the conditional chunk-integrity allegation. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 6.5 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The pinned requested-LoA accessor reads only the client note. ConditionalLoaAuthenticator skips a configured higher level when that requested value is lower. The enabled app-initiated KC_ACTION dispatcher reaches UpdateTotp, which validates the supplied new secret/token and adds it; an existing OTP triggers a device-label requirement, not proof of the old factor. The relevant hunks of the directly referenced backport compute the maximum of client and credential-action assurance based on configured flow and existing credentials. All three labeled spans support this scoped step-up failure. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 5 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

After selecting an enabled client and obtaining a nonempty trusted certificate chain, the authenticator searches every certificate for the configured subject or regex, then succeeds on any match. Under the explicitly matching-nonleaf assumption this authorizes the selected client although the leaf belongs elsewhere. The directly referenced repair matches certs[0] only. The broad source span contains the preceding guards and actual faulty match; the label correctly avoids claiming absent TLS chain validation. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 5.5 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The public lease RPC delegates to LeaseTimeToLive. At the verified pre-merge pin, Keys=true collects and returns lease key names without per-key read permission checks, for both local leader lookup and forwarded response. The advisory-linked merged PR metadata identifies the selected merge and its vulnerable parent; the retained component patch adds per-key IsRangePermitted and auth-revision checks. The accepted span is the actual unchecked disclosure operation, limited to names with RBAC enabled. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 3.1 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The revised label now explicitly requires credentials to be returned for the challenged foreign host. This resolves the initial material omission: the authorizer derives that host from the response and queries credentials(host), while the pinned ctr callback ignores host and supplies the configured credentials. Foreign descriptor URLs enter the same fetcher and authenticated retry path; the direct repair uses an auth-disabled copy for them. Both accepted fetcher spans are relevant. The original pre-packet finding is preserved separately, and this acceptance applies only to the corrected scope. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 6.1 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

Ordinary OCI signature/claim checks run before VerifyBundle. Bundle verification authenticates the Rekor SET; on the certificate path it checks time and payload hash, but bundleHash extracts the payload hash without comparing the recorded signature to the actual OCI signature. A valid matching-payload bundle from another signature can therefore falsely establish inclusion under the stated passing-crypto assumptions. The directly referenced repair compares signatures before accepting the bundle. The label does not assert signature forgery or payload-hash bypass. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 3.3 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The adapter selects a connection pool using URL/proxy without verification settings, then mutates pool certificate attributes through cert_verify. A previously established unverified TLS connection can remain reusable, so changing verify for the same session/host does not retroactively authenticate that connection. The advisory-linked merge and retained repair introduce verification settings into pool selection. Both the pool lookup and send/cert_verify ordering spans support the scoped reuse failure. Published severity provenance supports 3.1 5.6 (cna_cvss); differing authority ratings are retained in the case rather than recomputed.

The redirect loop calls rebuild_proxies before resending the prepared request. At the vulnerable pin, rebuild_proxies removes an old proxy header but unconditionally reconstructs Proxy-Authorization from the selected scheme's proxy credentials, including for HTTPS. The standard adapter forwards request.headers into the tunneled request. The patch specifically excludes HTTPS from this reconstruction. The label preserves authenticated-proxy, redirect and attacker-observable-destination assumptions; public CVE identity, exact repair/parent and CNA severity agree.

Retry's default removal set contains Authorization but not Cookie; PoolManager compares the redirect origin and removes only headers in that set before recursively requesting the destination. Explicit sensitive Cookie headers therefore persist across the stated cross-origin redirect. The patch adds Cookie to the default set. This does not assert browser cookie-jar behavior or override user-defined policies. Raw CVE, repair parent, and selected CNA metric match.

At the retained v8.5.1 release, the untrusted decoded header is passed to the key callback; explicitly configured algorithms suppress PEM-based inference, and verification checks algorithm membership before passing the same public-key bytes to jws.verify without key-type compatibility enforcement. The stated mixed-algorithm, poorly bound callback and known-public-key assumptions support the narrowed HMAC confusion claim. The causal repair is inferred through the retained release comparison: ecdf6 adds KeyObjects and rejects HS with non-secret keys; the advisory links a later release commit. This is not misrepresented as a first-parent mapping. CNA severity agrees.

The public parser only discards empty parsed keys, so it does not restore the lost distinction. The repair permits empty keys, anchors matching at the current offset and skips empty names. The label correctly requires affected browser/subdomain behavior and application selection of the malicious value, rather than universal browser impact. Direct mapping, first parent and CNA metric match.

The run/done path delivers the parsed body to the handler. The repair parses MIME type and distinguishes its essence from parameters. The label requires a JSON/preflight-dependent state-changing route, credential-bearing browser behavior and no independent CSRF defense. The direct CVE mapping, parent and CNA severity agree.

Certificate-chain construction uses the leaf NotBefore timestamp, while verifyInternal later calls CheckExpiry only with the leaf and a trusted timestamp or current time. CheckExpiry compares only that certificate's bounds. A custom chain whose issuer expires before its leaf can therefore pass these checks at a time after issuer expiry, assuming signature/policy/transparency checks otherwise pass. The patch carries the built issuing chain to CheckExpiry and checks each issuer at the observation time. The label explicitly excludes public Sigstore PKI. Direct repair mapping, parent and CNA severity agree.
